PRISON EXTORTION

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We piece together an elaborate extortion con involving fake cops run by professional criminals from inside a South African prison.

Unique Selling Point:
- DECONSTRUCTION OF A PRISONER EXTORTION CON
- FASCINATING INSIGHT INTO HOW THE CON WORKED
- INSIDERS SPILLTHE BEANS
- COPS DOING THEIR JOBS WELL

Summary:
You have to admire the ingenuity of criminals, an orange overall and time behind bars will not get them under – no Sir-ree!

Prisoners have been extorting people on the outside for years – from stock theft scams, to fake traffic fines to tow truck cons to sextortion rackets.

In this story, we deconstruct an elaborate con with videos, voice notes, insiders and an exclusive insight into the HAWKS investigation that lead to a crack down on a gang of prisoner conmen.


Further information:
This gang of prisoners recently met their match with Captain Jacques Loocke from the HAWKS in PTA. He managed to crack their con and built a case that lead to the conmen getting arrested for new criminals charges while behind bars.

These seemingly clever cons made around R1.5 million in just two months by blackmailing guys who dared to engage with some ladies of night. Yes! It’s complex ploy – they paid ladies of night for a names and numbers of some of their not so loyal clientele. The prisoners then pose as cops, who are on their way to arrest the clients on criminal charges related to sexual assault, and threats of exposure – unless they pay up.

The victims get such a big skrik they pay up not releasing there are a number of tell tale signs that would have cracked the con – simple things real cops don’t say or do. In our story we point these out.

Captain Loocke managed to trace the money flow, identifying victims and accomplices. He’s linked phone numbers and bank accounts – building a concrete case for the prosecution.

HOW DO THESE CONS GET THE CASH?
They’ve opened multiple online bank accounts with no proper FICA registration – allowing them to receive and funnel funds from their prison cells.
Undercover Element
We try to open an online bank account to show the loopholes in the South African banking system that continues to facilitate criminal activity.

INTERVIEWS
- CAPTAIN JACQUES LOOCKE – THE CASE
- LADY OF THE NIGHT – ACCOMPLICE – HIDDEN ID
- PRISONER SNITCH – HE’s STILL ON THE INSIDE
- LT COL PHILANI NKWALASE – POLICE PROTOCOL
- UNDERCOVER ELEMENt
- CONFRONT – BANK

** WE COULD TRY TO INTERVIEW A VICTIM – BUT I THINK THIS IS SO DONE, AND ANOTHER HIDDEN IDENTITY BECAUSE SHAME HE WASN’T TOO SHARP.

WE COULD USE THE DURATION MUCH BETTER BUILDING CAPTAIN LOOCKE INTO A CHARACTER, AND RETRACING BITS OF THE INVESTIGATION WITH HIM.

I FEEL A LINK WILL SUFFICE TO SPEAK ABOUT VICTIMS – THIS STORY IS NOT ABOUT THE VICTIMS, IT’s ABOUT THE CON

SCRIPT: PRISON EXTORTION

VO: South Africa. For criminals. A land of milk and honey… be it violent crime or complex cons – the opportunities are sadly endless ....

LINK: This story centers around ladies of the night. Counterfeit money, rape allegations, corrupt cops and extortion. But if there's one thing we've learned over the years is that everything is not always as it seems.

VO: It all starts with a call to a sex worker….whether the hook up followed or not, we can’t confirm.

But here is what we know happens next. The client gets a call within days of contacting the girl.

AUDIO NOTE - DISTORT VOICE SLIGHTLY
EXTORTIONIST: Okay. Mr. BEEP, there’s a case – two charges has been opened against you, sir. We arrested this woman with counterfeit money // She told us that she's a sex worker and the money she got on her, came from her last client. That client being you, sir. //

VO: Caller identification app, True Caller, shows the number is linked to a cop. And the allegations are about to take an even more sinister turn.

AUDIO NOTE - DISTORT VOICE SLIGHTLY
EXTORTIONIST: Where did you get the money that you paid this lady with? Because it was fake money and she's opening up a rape charge against you, sir?

VO: With the threat of imprisonment hanging over the so-called client, the cop offers the man a way out – pay up and you don’t get arrested.

ANNI: It's a game, a game of seeing how much profit you can gain from a victim.

VO: What criminologist, Professor Anni Hesselink, is describing is extortion.

ANNI: //It's like a hawk dove interaction communication processes which involves domination, fear. Humiliation, intimidation.

VO: But this is also blatant police corruption. HAWKS investigator Captain Jacques Loock picked up on the case.

CAPTAIN: //the investigation started with a complainant that laid a charged with us regarding a police official that was extorting him for money.
AUDIO NOTE - PAUSE BEFORE LINK
LINK: That is not the case. There are no cops running this racket. The extortionists are impersonating police officers. And this scam is being run from inside a correctional services facility From inside a prison.

AUDIO NOTE - PAUSE

VO: Captain Loock’s investigation led him here, to the Mabopane ODI Correctional Facility in Gauteng.

CAPTAIN: on the cell phone data, I could see that // all the calls day and night were coming from that area. And once I established that, I could see that this was not a police official extorting this person

VO: Pretending to be a cop is a deliberate move - it means the targets are unlikely to ask too many questions.

ANNI: This makes the persuasion and the control and the cohesion and the intimidation so much stronger and makes the victims so much more vulnerable to this type of crime//

VO: So committed to the con, the extortionist even forward victims this video clip.

AUDIO NOTE - DISTORT VOICE SLIGHTLY
EXTORTIONIST: Na werk is te laat, ons gaan dit nou moet afhandel ons reeds besig met die papier werk.
ENGLISH: After work is too late. We need to settle it now, we’re already busy with the paperwork.

VO: It is a real cop in the video clip – he is not involved . The audio’s been dubbed in - it’s the voice of one of the extortionists .

To make the con even more legit - a warrant of arrest is sent to the victim.

MASA: // would you WhatsApp a warrant of arrest?
CAPTAIN: Never. In this case, the procedures that are being followed by these impersonators is definitely not police procedure.

VO: The warrant of arrest is signed by a Captain Leon Bester. This is the linked caller profile. But that's not the man in the photo’s real name. No. This is actually Gerhard Prinsloo . He is not even in South AFrica, he lives in Ireland and resigned from the South African Police Service.

GERHARD: Low and behold there was my picture that was taken and the next minute I got a call for the investigating officer.
MASA: So for the record, Gerhard, you've never been involved in this extortion scam at all?
GERHARD: No, I was never.
MASA: You weren’t even in the country.
GERHARD: No, I was out of the country for over a year already.

VO: It’s an elaborate extortion racket with multiple roleplayers & different elements at play.

The first step is finding a target. This is where the ladies of the night come in.

Sex Workers are contacted via their online profiles by the extortionists, promising them cash for selling out their less favoured clients - from the no shows to the bad payers.

We spoke to a sensual massage therapist who asked us to hide her identity.

AUDIO NOTE - DISTORT VOICE
LADY: They said that they anyway deserve it, so might as well get money out of the guys. M8
MASA: How much did they offer you.
LADY: So, they basically said for each contact that they get money out of they would give me a certain percentage.. M9
MASA: And did they bug you a lot?
LADY: A lot, if I block them on one number, the next number the contact me on, is threats from the get go. M11

VO: This next clip is one of those threatening voice notes .

AUDIO NOTE - DISTORT VOICE SLIGHTLY
EXTORTIONIST: // jy is nou in dieper kak, jy is nou in dieper kak glo my – jy gaan exposed word, jy gaan alles verloor
ENGLISH: You’re in deeper sh*t now, you’re in deeper sh*t now, believe me. You will be exposed and you will lose everything.

VO: In the end most of the women offer up clients as extortion targets.

The convicts hone in on the target’s worst fears - threatening delays in investigation and DNA processing; arrest without bail and ironically time behind bars.

CAPTAIN: I don't think most of the time the issue of the rape is a problem for them because they know they didn't rape anyone. But proving it is a process and it's going to be a lengthy process and a lot of damage will be done if you do not pay this money.

VO: In this next clip, an extortionist can be heard.

AUDIO NOTE - DISTORT VOICE SLIGHTLY
EXTORTIONIST: If you're going to come to the station, you're going to make things very difficult because you are listed as a sex offender and I'm supposed to arrest you.

VO: To make the con a success - the inmates will need an operational bank account.

Captain Loock analysed a network of bank accounts used by the inmates for the cash they make from their crimes.

CAPTAIN: These accounts were all opened on a cell phone, on a banking app. //You need to have data and you need to take a photo of yourself and obviously provide your address //And yes, from there you can do Internet banking.
MASA: While sitting in prison.
CAPTAIN: While sitting in prison.

VO: These are some of the verification selfies the inmates submitted on the banking app. The addresses they used were fake.

MASA: Definitely a gentleman.
CAPTAIN: Yeah, it's a gentlemen's club. And six of the account’s addresses were. Linked to this address.

VO: We tested the process by downloading the app on a temporary phone, using an unrelated address and providing minimum information .
** ADDRESS PRONOUNCIATION

LINK: We managed to open an account without verifying any details in minutes. And just like that, we were able to transfer money in and out of the account immediately. No checks, no restrictions from the bank.

VO: Globally this is not an unusual business practice for digital banks. Nischal Mewalall represents the South African Banking Risk Information Centre.

NISCHAL: There is an expectation of you to come into the bank and formally fully activate the capability on the account.
MASA: I mean, a prisoner is never going to go inside the bank.
NISCHAL: Well, maybe it's never the intention of the prisoner to fully activate the entire capability of the account.

VO: While legally banking systems are not designed to prevent people from opening accounts or transacting, it does appear to create a window of opportunity for criminal syndicates.

NISCHAL: The laws are designed to ensure that we can identify who we're doing business with. Then you must keep records, then you should have a transaction monitoring system, and then you've got to report.

VO: But in this scam we’re investigating, it didn’t happen like that. Prisoners in orange uniforms opened bank accounts online, moved R1.3 million through two accounts in a matter of 2 and a half months and no one in the bank raised an eyebrow, until the HAWKS stepped in.

Statements show money flowing in and out of the accounts almost instantly.

CAPTAIN: There's the cell phone data that's being purchased, // a lot of cash sends // and then money that were paid over to other accounts, large amounts. //some of them are co-prisoners inside prison.

VO: The bank in question is Capitec . In a written response, it states that the bank is following procedure, it is FICA compliant and that account applications are monitored to the extent that even client clothing is analysed.

But, clearly these slipped through. As did the cellphones enabling this criminal activity.

We reached out to two sources and within an hour we were sent images from inside a prison - all taken by an inmate with his own personal smartphone. The prisoner taking the pics is serving time for armed robbery and attempted murder .

AUDIO NOTE - DISTORT VOICE SLIGHTLY
MASA: Where are you right now?
PRISONER: In Kgosi Mampuru
MASA: Kgosi Mampuru Prison.
PRISONER: Yah, yah. M2
MASA: The other prisoners. They also have phones.//
PRISONER: Yah, almost all the whole prison, you see.

AUDIO MOMENT… 1-2 seconds - dalk tralies was toe slaan…

VO: Singabakho Nxumalo is from the Department of Correctional Services.

MASA: Are Cell phones allowed in prison.
SINGABAKHO: Cell phones are not allowed to an extent that we define them as contraband.
MASA: I want to show you some images. These were sent to us yesterday. And if you look through here, I mean, what do you see?
SINGABAKHO: That's offender uniform.
MASA: Inside of?
SINGABAKHO: inside of a correctional facility.
MASA: And these were taken with a cell phone?
SINGABAKHO: Yes, with a mobile phone.

VO: It seems it's an open secret, and even if a prison warden catches you, it’s not such a biggie.

AUDIO NOTE - DISTORT VOICE SLIGHTLY
PRISONER: Sometimes you know, when they find you charging, they find a phone in your possession – some they took, some give them money they don’t take it. M6

AUDIO MOMENT… GLITCH TRANSITION

MASA: Is it safe to say that these criminals are actually sharper THAN you as a department
SINGABAKHO: The modus operandi will always change. // it becomes difficult when you have some within your force who work against you. Hence it's important that we get rid of those people. we can no longer tolerate that.
MASA: But when? Because already in 2014, Carte Blanche did a story about these cell phones in prisons. Here we are sitting almost a decade later
SINGABAKHO: It's something that we can never give up on. //

VO: But it seems a life of crime is something these inmates can’t give up on either.

ANNI: // It's a mindset. They are not in prison to be rehabilitated. //They get us a psychological kick out of it. Like I am in prison and I can still operate and no means of control will be able to stop me from recommitting and re-offending. Crime.

VO: Based on all the evidence, a raid was done at Mabopane Prison. 36 cellphones were confiscated and four prisoners were charged with extortion and the impersonation of police officials.

Nxumalo concedes - it’s an ongoing battle

AUDIO NOTE - LEAVE 2 SECODNS OF MUSIC

MASA: THE Ideal solution. HERE IS that prisoners should not be having cell phones.
SINGABAKHO: We are looking // at other means as a legislative wise to say, should we be allowed to, you know, block the signal in particular areas // But these are the things that we are exploring.

VO: Captain Loock’s investigation is ongoing.

CAPTAIN: Investigation of crime is a systematic search for the truth. So we will go on. It's like a tennis game. If you hit us, we will hit back. We will keep on going until we disable this modus operandi.M21

END ON VISUALS

NISCHAL: Well, maybe it's never the intention of the prisoner to fully activate the entire capability of the account. VO: While legally banking systems are not designed to prevent people from opening accounts or transacting, it does appear to create a window of opportunity for criminal syndicates. NISCHAL: The laws are designed to ensure that we can identify who we're doing business with. Then you must keep records, then you should have a transaction monitoring system, and then you've got to report. VO: But in this scam we’re investigating, it didn’t happen like that. Prisoners in orange uniforms opened bank accounts online, moved R1.3 million through two accounts in a matter of 2 and a half months and no one in the bank raised an eyebrow, until the HAWKS stepped in. Statements show money flowing in and out of the accounts almost instantly. CAPTAIN: There's the cell phone data that's being purchased, // a lot of cash sends // and then money that were paid over to other accounts, large amounts. //some of them are co-prisoners inside prison. VO: The bank in question is Capitec . In a written response, it states that the bank is following procedure, it is FICA compliant and that account applications are monitored to the extent that even client clothing is analysed. But, clearly these slipped through. As did the cellphones enabling this criminal activity. We reached out to two sources and within an hour we were sent images from inside a prison - all taken by an inmate with his own personal smartphone. The prisoner taking the pics is serving time for armed robbery and attempted murder . AUDIO NOTE - DISTORT VOICE SLIGHTLY MASA: Where are you right now? PRISONER: In Kgosi Mampuru MASA: Kgosi Mampuru Prison. PRISONER: Yah, yah. M2 MASA: The other prisoners. They also have phones.// PRISONER: Yah, almost all the whole prison, you see. AUDIO MOMENT… 1-2 seconds - dalk tralies was toe slaan… VO: Singabakho Nxumalo is from the Department of Correctional Services. MASA: Are Cell phones allowed in prison. SINGABAKHO: Cell phones are not allowed to an extent that we define them as contraband. MASA: I want to show you some images. These were sent to us yesterday. And if you look through here, I mean, what do you see? SINGABAKHO: That's offender uniform. MASA: Inside of? SINGABAKHO: inside of a correctional facility. MASA: And these were taken with a cell phone? SINGABAKHO: Yes, with a mobile phone. VO: It seems it's an open secret, and even if a prison warden catches you, it’s not such a biggie. AUDIO NOTE - DISTORT VOICE SLIGHTLY PRISONER: Sometimes you know, when they find you charging, they find a phone in your possession – some they took, some give them money they don’t take it. M6 AUDIO MOMENT… GLITCH TRANSITION MASA: Is it safe to say that these criminals are actually sharper THAN you as a department SINGABAKHO: The modus operandi will always change. // it becomes difficult when you have some within your force who work against you. Hence it's important that we get rid of those people. we can no longer tolerate that. MASA: But when? Because already in 2014, Carte Blanche did a story about these cell phones in prisons. Here we are sitting almost a decade later SINGABAKHO: It's something that we can never give up on. // VO: But it seems a life of crime is something these inmates can’t give up on either. ANNI: // It's a mindset. They are not in prison to be rehabilitated. //They get us a psychological kick out of it. Like I am in prison and I can still operate and no means of control will be able to stop me from recommitting and re-offending. Crime. VO: Based on all the evidence, a raid was done at Mabopane Prison. 36 cellphones were confiscated and four prisoners were charged with extortion and the impersonation of police officials. Nxumalo concedes - it’s an ongoing battle AUDIO NOTE - LEAVE 2 SECODNS OF MUSIC MASA: THE Ideal solution. HERE IS that prisoners should not be having cell phones. SINGABAKHO: We are looking // at other means as a legislative wise to say, should we be allowed to, you know, block the signal in particular areas // But these are the things that we are exploring. VO: Captain Loock’s investigation is ongoing. CAPTAIN: Investigation of crime is a systematic search for the truth. So we will go on. It's like a tennis game. If you hit us, we will hit back. We will keep on going until we disable this modus operandi.M21 END ON VISUALS PROMOS PROMO 1 - 11 SECONDS VO: Rape Allegations. Fake Cops. Extortion. It’s an elaborate scam raking in millions of rands pulled off by professional criminals from inside a South African prison. PROMO 2 - 21 SECONDS VO: Imagine being extorted for a crime you didn’t commit EXTORTIONIST: If you're going to come to the station, you're going to make things very difficult because you are listed as a sex offender and I'm supposed to arrest you / VO: Only to find out, the extortionist isn’t a cop but rather a convict calling you from inside a prison. We deconstruct this complex con. PROMO 3 - 21 SECONDS VO: Next level intimidation tactics reel in millions of rands in a complex extortion racket. ANNI: It's a game, a game of seeing how much profit you can gain from a victim. It's like a hawk dove interaction communication processes. metadata.Summary: You have to admire the ingenuity of criminals, an orange overall and time behind bars will not get them under – no Sir-ree! Prisoners have been extorting people on the outside for years – from stock theft scams, to fake traffic fines to tow truck cons to sextortion rackets. In this story, we deconstruct an elaborate con with videos, voice notes, insiders and an exclusive insight into the HAWKS investigation that lead to a crack down on a gang of prisoner conmen.
metadata.Further information: This gang of prisoners recently met their match with Captain Jacques Loocke from the HAWKS in PTA. He managed to crack their con and built a case that lead to the conmen getting arrested for new criminals charges while behind bars. These seemingly clever cons made around R1.5 million in just two months by blackmailing guys who dared to engage with some ladies of night. Yes! It’s complex ploy – they paid ladies of night for a names and numbers of some of their not so loyal clientele. The prisoners then pose as cops, who are on their way to arrest the clients on criminal charges related to sexual assault, and threats of exposure – unless they pay up. The victims get such a big skrik they pay up not releasing there are a number of tell tale signs that would have cracked the con – simple things real cops don’t say or do. In our story we point these out. Captain Loocke managed to trace the money flow, identifying victims and accomplices. He’s linked phone numbers and bank accounts – building a concrete case for the prosecution. HOW DO THESE CONS GET THE CASH? They’ve opened multiple online bank accounts with no proper FICA registration – allowing them to receive and funnel funds from their prison cells. Undercover Element We try to open an online bank account to show the loopholes in the South African banking system that continues to facilitate criminal activity. INTERVIEWS - CAPTAIN JACQUES LOOCKE – THE CASE - LADY OF THE NIGHT – ACCOMPLICE – HIDDEN ID - PRISONER SNITCH – HE’s STILL ON THE INSIDE - LT COL PHILANI NKWALASE – POLICE PROTOCOL - UNDERCOVER ELEMENt - CONFRONT – BANK ** WE COULD TRY TO INTERVIEW A VICTIM – BUT I THINK THIS IS SO DONE, AND ANOTHER HIDDEN IDENTITY BECAUSE SHAME HE WASN’T TOO SHARP. WE COULD USE THE DURATION MUCH BETTER BUILDING CAPTAIN LOOCKE INTO A CHARACTER, AND RETRACING BITS OF THE INVESTIGATION WITH HIM. I FEEL A LINK WILL SUFFICE TO SPEAK ABOUT VICTIMS – THIS STORY IS NOT ABOUT THE VICTIMS, IT’s ABOUT THE CON
